title: Recoil transport and environmental exposure of black-hole merger remnants
abstract: Black-hole mergers in stellar clusters can leave remnants moving through their hosts after receiving gravitational-wave recoil. Remaining gravitationally bound does not determine how soon a remnant enters a dense region or how much time it spends there. Predicting this motion requires a stellar environment that consistently supplies gravity, collisional drift, and velocity diffusion. We formulate merger-conditioned transport and define finite-region residence and species-resolved exposure on its trajectories. Public observations and published multimass-model posteriors for six Galactic clusters supply conditional reference hosts and a joint-parameter sensitivity pilot. Independent checks connect their mass distributions, potentials, velocity moments and projected tracer profiles to local anisotropic scattering calculations. Black holes can dominate formal central diffusion in both low-count and massive-reservoir models, while the radial extent of that contribution differs strongly. Published model variation and applicability limitations prevent a selected sparse population from being treated as an observationally secure background. Galactic reference orbits and static controls separate conditional tidal scales from sufficient domains for neglecting external forces. These calculations identify environments and spatial regions for a subsequent test of the continuous scattering approximation. They do not establish its failure or provide calibrated remnant residence distributions.
